findings.claim: renovate/v* tag series unprotected; attacker with push access can re-point preset tag to malicious commit, cascading adversarial Renovate config to all estate adopters.
findings.evidence: scripts/configure-020f-renovate-tag-protection.sh L63-83: creates ruleset 'scp-tag-protection-renovate-v' on refs/tags/renovate/v* with enforcement='active', rules=[deletion, non_fast_forward, update], bypass_actors=[]. Exact structural match to configure-020j-protections.sh L120-140 scp-tag-protection-v ruleset — same three rules, same enforcement level, empty bypass_actors. Idempotent: existing-ID check at L56-58 prevents duplicate creation.
findings.impact: CLOSED — same protection regime as 020J v* namespace now covers renovate/v* namespace. No residual gap in rule set shape.
findings.mitigation: N/A (closed). See NEW-R2-SAFE-001 for residual TOCTOU in post-merge execution order introduced by this fix.

findings.claim: renovate.json extends preset without tag pin; floating HEAD exposes SCP self-consumer to undiscovered regressions on any future commit to renovate/default.json on main.
findings.evidence: renovate.json L5: 'github>jrnb2024/standards-control-plane-//renovate/default' has no #<tag> anchor. DISPATCH-NOTE.md L88: TF-020F-001 names this explicitly with concrete next step ('post-merge tag-cut + ~5-line PR'). CODEOWNERS L37: renovate/** @jrnb2024 is the interim PR-level gate against unreviewed preset changes.
findings.impact: DEFERRED — named TF-020F-001, not silent descope. No-silent-descope rule is satisfied: the item is tracked, named, timed, and the interim gate is live.
findings.mitigation: TF-020F-001: update renovate.json extends to 'github>jrnb2024/standards-control-plane-//renovate/default#renovate/v1.0.0' once TF-020F-003 tag-cut is complete.

findings.claim: Adopter packageRule could override automerge=false in the preset, enabling auto-promotion of malicious supply-chain updates without human review.
findings.evidence: renovate/default.json L9: root automerge=false. L22 (scp-federation packageRule): automerge=false asserted a second time. L3 description: 'Adopters MUST NOT add packageRules that override the SCP federation primitive's automerge=false.' To flip automerge an adopter would need to either (a) NAME the 'scp-federation-primitive' groupName in a new packageRule — which is conspicuous — or (b) supply a broader matchPackageNames that re-matches the same package after this rule in the array, which Renovate last-rule-wins semantics would allow but which again requires an explicit targeted override.
findings.impact: CLOSED — dual-layer automerge=false (root + packageRule) plus description warning. The defence-in-depth is adequate; a careless adopter cannot accidentally enable automerge.

findings.claim: ignoreUnstable=false globally causes RC bumps for all dependencies, not just the federation primitive, regressing adopter repos to RC builds.
findings.evidence: renovate/default.json L14: ignoreUnstable=true at root (conservative global default, blocks RC bumps estate-wide). L21: ignoreUnstable=false inside scp-federation packageRule (explicit per-package opt-in for jrnb2024/standards-control-plane- only). v1.0.0-rc.1 is valid semver by spec; versioningTemplate='semver' (customManagers[0]) correctly parses it. Renovate packageRule settings override root for matched packages — only the federation primitive receives RC bump proposals. Documented intent confirmed at packageRule description L17: 'adopters DO want rc.N proposals so they can canary in advance of GA.'
findings.impact: CLOSED — global posture is stable-only; RC opt-in is scoped to the federation primitive by design and matches documented intent.

findings.claim: config:recommended is a Mend-controlled floating ref; a future Renovate-org change could silently flip automerge or other safety-critical settings.
findings.evidence: renovate/default.json L9: explicit automerge=false at root takes precedence over any config:recommended automerge change. Pinning config:recommended is impractical (Renovate built-in, no semver pin mechanism). L3 description documents the trust assumption and automerge-override warning. Partial closure acknowledged in FIX-ROUND-1 and assessed as acceptable trade-off.
findings.impact: CLOSED (partial, acceptable) — automerge surface is hardened via explicit root override. Other config:recommended settings (schedule, rangeStrategy) could still shift on Mend changes; assessed as lower-risk surface and documented in description.
findings.mitigation: N/A (partially closed, acceptable). No action required; monitor Renovate changelog for config:recommended changes affecting non-automerge settings.

findings.claim: TOCTOU window: DISPATCH-NOTE.md post-merge steps cut the renovate/v1.0.0 tag BEFORE applying the tag-protection ruleset, leaving the newly pushed tag unprotected for the seconds between the two commands.
findings.evidence: DISPATCH-NOTE.md L73-83 post-merge steps: step 1 is 'git tag -a renovate/v1.0.0 ... && git push origin renovate/v1.0.0'; step 2 is './scripts/configure-020f-renovate-tag-protection.sh'. GitHub Repository Rulesets protect a ref PATTERN regardless of whether any matching refs exist at ruleset-creation time — applying the ruleset first would protect the tag the moment it is pushed. The current order inverts this safety property: the tag is live and unprotected during the inter-command window.
findings.impact: An actor with push access (e.g., via a compromised personal access token in the operator's shell session, or a GitHub Actions workflow with write-tag permission) could force-push renovate/v1.0.0 to a malicious commit in the seconds between step 1 and step 2. Once the ruleset is applied the tag becomes immutable, but a tampered tag already pushed would persist and cascade to any adopter whose Renovate runs against it before the tamper is detected. Practical risk is low (single-operator estate, consecutive commands), but the window is real.
findings.mitigation: Reverse the post-merge order in DISPATCH-NOTE.md: (1) run configure-020f-renovate-tag-protection.sh first — idempotent and safe to apply against an empty renovate/v* namespace; (2) then cut and push the renovate/v1.0.0 tag. The GitHub ruleset pattern 'refs/tags/renovate/v*' enforces protection on the tag the instant it is created, eliminating the window.

findings.claim: configure-020f-renovate-tag-protection.sh uses an unquoted heredoc (<<JSON, not <<'JSON'), expanding $RULESET_NAME and $TAG_PATTERN directly into the JSON request body without sanitization; a tainted environment variable can inject arbitrary JSON fields. The post-creation verification does not confirm enforcement=active or rule completeness, so a poisoned ruleset passes the verification ✓ check.
findings.evidence: scripts/configure-020f-renovate-tag-protection.sh L63: heredoc opener <<JSON (unquoted) causes bash to expand ${RULESET_NAME} and ${TAG_PATTERN} into the payload before passing it to 'gh api --input -'. Attack example: SCP_RENOVATE_RULESET_NAME='evil","enforcement":"disabled","x":"' produces a JSON body with enforcement=disabled while the 'name' field is set to 'evil'. Post-creation verification at L87-94 queries by name and checks only that final_id is non-empty — it does NOT inspect enforcement, rules array, or bypass_actors. A disabled ruleset with the expected name passes verification and logs '✓'. The same verification gap exists in configure-020j-protections.sh (pre-existing pattern), confirming it was not introduced here, but the unquoted heredoc in the new 020F script compounds the risk.
findings.impact: A tainted env var — from a compromised shell session, a misconfigured CI pipeline running this script, or a social-engineering attack on the operator — could silently create a disabled ruleset that closes CRIT-SAFE-001 on paper while leaving the renovate/v* namespace fully unprotected. The log output would be indistinguishable from a correct run. Practical risk is low (admin-only manual script, single-operator estate, safe defaults) but the verification gap makes the failure mode silent.
findings.mitigation: (1) Replace heredoc interpolation with jq --arg construction to structurally separate data from JSON structure: jq -n --arg n "$RULESET_NAME" --arg p "refs/tags/$TAG_PATTERN" '{name:$n,target:"tag",enforcement:"active",conditions:{ref_name:{include:[$p],exclude:[]}},rules:[{type:"deletion"},{type:"non_fast_forward"},{type:"update"}],bypass_actors:[]}' | gh api -X POST "repos/${REPO}/rulesets" -H 'Accept: application/vnd.github+json' --input - (2) Extend verification to assert enforcement=active: gh api -X GET "repos/${REPO}/rulesets/${final_id}" | jq -e '.enforcement == "active"' || { echo 'verification failed: enforcement is not active' >&2; exit 1; } Apply the same fix to configure-020j-protections.sh for consistency.

probe_results.item_10_prhourlylimit_zero: CORRECT — Renovate treats prHourlyLimit=0 as 'no limit' (unlimited PRs per hour), not 'zero PRs per hour'. Renovate documentation: 'Set this to 0 to disable the hourly limit.' The vulnerabilityAlerts.prHourlyLimit=0 fix correctly removes the throttle on security alert PRs. automerge=false inside vulnerabilityAlerts ensures human review is still required. No finding.
probe_results.item_7_toctou_window: REAL — tag-cut before ruleset application creates a brief unprotected window. Flagged as NEW-R2-SAFE-001 (MIN). Mitigation: reverse the execution order in DISPATCH-NOTE.md post-merge steps.
probe_results.item_8_rc_semver: CORRECT BY DESIGN — v1.0.0-rc.1 is valid semver per spec; versioningTemplate=semver parses it correctly. ignoreUnstable=false in the scp-federation packageRule overrides the root ignoreUnstable=true for jrnb2024/standards-control-plane- only, enabling RC bump proposals for that package. This matches the documented intent in the packageRule description. No finding.
probe_results.item_9_description_visibility: ACCEPTABLE AWARENESS GAP — description field is visible in the Renovate dashboard (developer.mend.io) but is not surfaced in PR bodies. The automerge warning is advisory; the primary control is structural (dual automerge=false assertions at root and packageRule). The awareness gap does not weaken the security posture. No finding.

structured_review.summary: R2 safety/bypass review of 020F post fix-round-1. All six R1 findings are resolved: CRIT-SAFE-001 closed (configure-020f-renovate-tag-protection.sh mirrors 020J ruleset shape identically), MAJ-SAFE-002 explicitly deferred as named TF-020F-001 with CODEOWNERS interim gate, MAJ-SAFE-003 through MAJ-SAFE-006 all closed. Two new MIN findings surface from R2 probing introduced by the fix: (1) NEW-R2-SAFE-001 — post-merge instructions in DISPATCH-NOTE.md cut the renovate/v1.0.0 tag before applying the protection ruleset, creating a brief TOCTOU window; mitigation is to reverse the order so the ruleset protects the pattern before the tag is pushed; (2) NEW-R2-SAFE-002 — configure-020f-renovate-tag-protection.sh uses an unquoted heredoc expanding env vars into the JSON body without sanitization, and the post-creation verification checks only ruleset name existence rather than enforcement=active or rule completeness, meaning a tainted env var could silently produce a disabled ruleset that passes the ✓ check; mitigation is jq --arg construction plus enforcement assertion in verification. No new CRIT or MAJ findings. Merge-unblocked. Both MINs should be addressed in the follow-up PR that closes TF-020F-001.
